["What people are not understanding is that AI frontier training + chip development + robot hardware working together is the key. The Chinese are very far away. This is why you see the Chinese robots performing preprogrammed movement and looking impressive but the immediately falling over as soon and any slightest wrinkle is introduced. It is the reason that Optimus is very far ahead. They might look good doing preprogrammed kung fu on tv but are light years away from real world utility. I live in Beijing and have a few Chinese engineers and PHDs in my friends group. They ALL agree with what I just wrote. The Chinese are masters at making things look all shiny and impressive on the outside but fall apart inside and this is not different and the West currently has inferiority complex when it think of China's manufacturing capabilities. The Chinese move very fast and copy fast and well but that's going to win the AI robot race...actual AI robots not dumb robots with the letter AI placed in front.", "Now come on... In contrast to AI systems these humanoid robots only fail in certain situations. And yes, getting those final 10% right often takes 90% of the work. So they still need quite some time and money. 
- Never the less: 
As a German who grew up in a country that once valued its innovative engineering tradition, I definitely admire how far the Chinese engineers have already come in the field of robotics. I wish we would be anywhere near that... Just like with cars our industry has been dormant for decades now thinking that repetition is all it takes to build great products. Thus now the Chinese aren't that far away from being for robotics what we used to be for cars for so long. And just like that one CEO said: They haven't gotten to their ChatGPT moment yet, but I believe they will get there... maybe not in the next three or five years, but from my point of view some will be there within a decade.
- Thus I say: 
These are no fails, these are the the next steps to be taken. 
Congratulations and respect to those engineers.", 'All we can see in china so far are remote controlled "toy" robots. They are doing endurance, agility, stability and balance research at the moment .. Most of the robots have no brains and cannot fullfill any complex task autonomously. To build the brain that is capable of understanding the world, the physics and the manipulation of objects inside this real world is one of the most complex things.
by the way .. China pays a lot of subsidies for the development of autonomous humanoid robots .. because they use the tax-payers money more efficient in the chinese government. They are building up a whole industry for the production of humanoids, because they know how important those robots will be in the future ( to be used in future wars as armed robots or policing and monitoring the streets of china .. total control of the people and their public actions is the desired achievement of the dictatorship in China ).     

Elon Musk with his company Tesla for example is working hard on camera based autonomous navigation, using the same software in their optimus robots as well as in their Tesla cars. We are only weeks or months away from publishing Tesla Optimus Generation 3. At the moment the only real competitors of Tesla Optimus are the humanoid robots Figure 03 and the "new" Atlas from Boston.
Without a brain that understands the world they cannot even fullfill tasks that humans can do easily. May be it is better this way .. humans keep their jobs as long as possible ....  unemployment will be the biggest problem in the very close future !  Revolution will be the outcome !']
